page: Microsoft Azure L48as_v3 is a virtual machine instance belonging to the LASv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor, which operates at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supporting simultaneous multithreading with 2.0 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It includes 12012 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not feature any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong CPU performance, with both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests scoring in the top 25%. The Passmark CPU score and Passmark CPU encryption test also rank in the top 25%, alongside strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core and image processing metrics. However, memory bandwidth remains in the middle 50% for both small cached blocks and large uncached read/write operations. Similarly, database operations, Redis SET operations, static web serving throughput, and LLM inference speeds for 135M and 7B models fall within the average performance tier.

With its high local storage capacity of over 12 TB and a balanced 8 GB of memory per vCPU, the L48as_v3 offers high resource density for storage-heavy workloads. The qualitative cost efficiency is driven by the combination of dedicated AMD EPYC processing power and substantial local storage, reducing the need for external storage attachments. This configuration is suitable for large-scale databases, data warehousing, memory-intensive data processing, and multi-threaded file decompression tasks where local storage speed and capacity are critical.
